subject: humanities
passage: Swans have glided along the canals of Bruges, in Belgium, for more than five centuries, and the city tells a story to explain why. In 1488, the townspeople rose up against their ruler, Maximilian of Austria, and executed his counselor Pieter Lanchals. Lanchals, whose family name means "long ______ had a swan on his coat of arms. According to the legend, Maximilian punished the city by ordering it to keep swans on its waters forever. Historians doubt that any such order was ever given, but the birds remain, and the city still cares for them.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Whose family name means 'long neck'" is extra information about Lanchals that opens with a comma after "Lanchals," so a comma must close it before the verb "had." In American English, that comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.
explanation.A: Correct. The comma closes the extra information and sits inside the closing quotation mark, as American usage requires.
explanation.B: Incorrect. In American English, a comma at the end of quoted words goes inside the closing quotation mark, not after it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Lanchals" from its verb "had," and it is not part of the quoted words.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The comma after "Lanchals" opens a pair, so a matching comma must close the extra information before "had."
